title: Which file or directory?
description: Match a question about the system to the file or directory that answers it.

cards.prompt: Mira wants the list of user accounts with their user IDs, home directories and login shells.
cards.why: `/etc/passwd` has one line per account: name, `x`, UID, GID, comment, home and shell. It is readable by everyone.

cards.prompt: Which file keeps the password hashes, readable only by root?
cards.why: Since the hashes moved out of `/etc/passwd` (where an `x` stands now), they live in `/etc/shadow` with strict permissions.

cards.prompt: Where does Mira find which users are members of the group `artists`?
cards.why: `/etc/group` has one line per group: name, `x`, GID and the list of members.

cards.prompt: Ada wants fixed name-to-address pairs that the system checks before it asks a DNS server.
cards.why: `/etc/hosts` maps names to addresses by hand. `/etc/nsswitch.conf` only sets the order of the lookup sources.

cards.prompt: Which file lists the DNS servers (`nameserver` lines) that the machine asks?
cards.why: `/etc/resolv.conf` names the DNS servers, one `nameserver` line each. `/etc/hosts` holds fixed pairs instead.

cards.prompt: Which file holds just the name of this machine?
cards.why: `/etc/hostname` contains the machine’s name and nothing else. The guest’s name is `tuxpixel`.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to know which distribution and release this machine runs.
cards.why: `/etc/os-release` names the distribution and its version. `/proc/version` describes the kernel, not the distribution.

cards.prompt: Which file describes the processor: model, cores and speed?
cards.why: `/proc/cpuinfo` is built by the kernel when you read it, and lists each CPU core. It is not stored on disk.

cards.prompt: Which file shows the total and free memory, as the kernel sees it?
cards.why: `/proc/meminfo` lists memory figures such as `MemTotal` and `MemFree`. The command `free` reads the same numbers.

cards.prompt: Where do services such as the build daemon normally write their log files?
cards.why: `/var/log` holds the logs, for example `syslog` and `auth.log` on Debian. `/etc` holds settings, and `/proc` shows live kernel data.

cards.prompt: Jonas needs a scratch directory that every user may write to and that is cleared when the machine restarts.
cards.why: `/tmp` is for short-lived files and is emptied at reboot (or sooner). `/var/tmp` keeps its files across reboots.

cards.prompt: Ada wants a temporary directory whose files must still be there after a reboot.
cards.why: `/var/tmp` is the temporary directory that survives a reboot. `/tmp` does not promise that.

cards.prompt: Mira wants to discard the output of a command completely, so she redirects it to a device file.
cards.why: `/dev/null` throws away everything written to it. `/dev/zero` and `/dev/urandom` are sources: they produce zeros and random bytes when read.

cards.prompt: Which device file delivers an endless stream of zero bytes when read?
cards.why: `/dev/zero` gives zero bytes forever. `/dev/null` gives nothing at all, and `/dev/urandom` gives random bytes.

cards.prompt: Which directory holds the kernel and the initial RAM disk that the machine needs to start?
cards.why: `/boot` has the kernel (`vmlinuz-…`), the initial RAM disk and the boot loader’s files.

cards.prompt: What is the home directory of the administrator account `root`?
cards.why: Root’s home is `/root`, outside `/home`. The directory `/` is the top of the whole tree, which is something else again.

cards.prompt: Which file gets copied into a new user’s home when `useradd -m` creates it, as a template?
cards.why: `/etc/skel` holds the default files, such as `.bashrc`, that every new home directory starts with.

cards.prompt: Where is it configured which users may run commands as root with `sudo`?
cards.why: `/etc/sudoers` holds the rules for `sudo`. On Debian, membership of the group `sudo` is allowed there too.

cards.prompt: Ada wants to log in to the build server with her key and no password. Which file on the server lists the public keys that are accepted?
cards.why: The server reads `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` of the account you log in to. `known_hosts` is on the client and remembers servers, and `id_ed25519` is the private key.

cards.prompt: Which directory holds programs meant for the system administrator, such as `fdisk` and `ip`?
cards.why: The `s` in `sbin` stands for system. On a current Debian, `/sbin` is only a link to `/usr/sbin`.
